title: Typing / in Ask lists the commands you can run
goal: In the Ask composer, typing / turns it into the command list the mock shows: every menu command by name, filtered as you type, and Return runs the one picked, so a sentence you ask and a command you run go through the same box. After a run, the Agent group lists what changed, and clicking a change picks that layer on the canvas.
notes: Left out of the first Ask slice (ask-in-the-app-runs-on-a-local-model-with-no-mod). Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/agent-generate-wt.html (#agentChanges, .askcmd .cplist in docs/design/mocks/shared/dist/photonz-ds.js askPalHTML). Commands: AppCommandTable (PhotonzCore) with EditorState.run(_:) and canRun. Composer: AskComposerOverlay in Sources/Photonz/Agent/AskViews.swift; Agent group: AgentPanel.
acceptance: In the Ask composer (title bar Ask button or Command K), typing / shows a filtered list of commands with their menu names, as the mock agent-generate-wt.html step 1 shows
Return or a click on a row runs that command on the document, one undo step, and the list closes
Clicking a request's row in the Agent group (the rows ask-makes-the-change-straight-away-and-each-chan builds) picks what it changed on the canvas and in Layers
A walk proves both with the pointer, at Next defaults
The composer stays up over the window after Ask, showing what was asked and whether it is still working, as the mock's chat does, without covering the Agent group (today it closes as soon as you ask)

manager 2026-10-22: today the composer opens over the top edge of the picture (queue/manager/shots/2026-10-22-ask-needs-ollama-typed.png, about 20 pt over a settings screenshot the request asks to measure). If this task keeps the composer up after Ask, it must not sit over the document being changed (the never-cover rule in UX-PATTERNS): park it where it covers neither the canvas content nor the Agent group, and say where in the audit.

Before building, trying to break it: (1) row click already works (AskSession.pickChange, prior task), so that item needs proof, not code. (2) 34 commands take required arguments: a bare row for Align or Speed would do nothing on Return, a control that does nothing. So each choice is its own row (Align Left, Speed 50%), rows ending in an ellipsis open their own sheet as the menu does, and anything else cannot run from one row and is left out. (3) Commands that open a sheet cannot sit under a dimming composer, so a run closes the overlay. (4) Keeping the composer focused after Ask would send Command Z to the text field and not the document, so the keyboard goes back to the canvas. (5) The mock's own left dock is the parking place: it takes layout room, so it can never cover the picture or the Agent group.
owns these walks: ask-slash-lists-commands-walk, ask-stays-up-after-asking-walk, ask-narrow-window-has-no-dock-walk

Chose the mock's left dock over a floating card for where the conversation stays after Ask, because it takes layout room and so cannot cover the picture or the Agent group at any zoom; a floating card has no free corner once a picture fills the view.
Chose to close the composer after a / command over the mock's staying open, because a sheet a command opens cannot sit under the dim and the result should not be dimmed.
Chose to give the keyboard back to the canvas after Ask over keeping the field focused as the mock does, because Command Z would otherwise undo the text field and not the request.
Chose to give a / command that changed the document a row in the Agent group, no thumbs, reading the goal's 'after a run, the Agent group lists what changed'. Put as a question in the audit.

Older walks on this change: ask-shows-the-agent-group (5, updated to expect the dock's field), ask-queues, ask-cancels, ask-rows, ask-hero, ask-is-command, ask-stops ok. ask-row-thumbs timed out once at its 300s limit (step 8, a cold run), then passed 248s on the same build: a thin margin, not a fix. ask-stops fails when it is first to use a cold model, with or without this change (baseline run), so it is filed apart. Only 15 walks of those that send a request were run; the rest of the 30 come round in the rotating check.

Typing / in Ask lists every command by name, filtered as you type; Return, arrows or a click run it as one undo step and close the list (AskCommandList in PhotonzCore, AskCommandsList in AskViews). After Ask the conversation stays up in the mock's left dock beside the canvas (AskConversationDock), covering neither the picture nor the Agent group; Command K floats it back. Clicking a row picks what it made. Verified: Scripts/test.sh green, 3 new walks at Next defaults with no flags. Audit: queue/audits/2026-11-04-typing-in-ask-lists-the-commands-you-can-run.json
